retrieved_synopses: Attendant serving as the front desk for the House of Grief. Recognises Shadowheart and urges her to enter the room beyond and submit to the Mapping of the heart, and beyond it, her return to the Sharran grotto.

Morann is a sentry posted at the door to the House of Grief’s Mapping Room, a controlled chamber whose access is managed by attendants at the front. Off‑screen the attendant handles permissions, paperwork, and whatever “price” the House demands; the player may already have authorization or must bargain for entry. Morann’s lines show he’s duty‑bound and inclined to enforce procedure, but will relent if shown proof, persuaded, or intimidated. The location is tied to Shar‑related business in the cluster contexts, so who may enter and why matters to characters like Shadowheart and to the broader temple conflicts.
One-node dialog for the guard at the House of Grief. The guard presents herself as an usher/greeter for the House of Grief - outwardly friendly and welcoming, while in truth acting as sentry.

The player is standing at the entrance of the House of Grief — a Shar-affiliated shrine — where Griefguard Wilbur serves as a sentry who plays the part of a gentle usher. His lines are scripted, single-node greetings meant to comfort, shepherd, and sometimes flatter visitors into the temple’s care rather than start a full conversation. Depending on tone he can be soothing and pastoral (“only you can decide…”) or openly sycophantic and loyal to Lady Shar, using praise to curry favor or recruit. If companions (like Shadowheart) have already discovered or read about a Shar temple and a “shadow curse,” those facts will color how the player and party interpret Wilbur’s invocation of Shar.
Serves as the front desk for the House of Grief. Encourages the player to partake of their services in exchange for a fee. Secretly a Sharran agent seeking to lure in the unwitting.
context: You are at the door to the House of Grief’s Mapping Room where Morann stands sentry; the Mapping chamber is a controlled Shar‑affiliated space and entry is governed by the attendants at the front desk. Off‑screen the attendant handles permissions, paperwork and whatever “price” the House demands, so the player may already have authorization or must bargain or pay to gain access. Morann is duty‑bound and insists on procedure — he will refuse entry unless shown proof of permission, persuaded, or intimidated, but can relent if satisfied. If companions (for example Shadowheart) or prior actions have tied the party to the temple, that context will shape how both attendant and sentry respond.
